summary: Buso Renkin (26 eps, Xebec 2006-07) is a complete, essentially 1:1 adaptation of the whole 10-volume manga: no filler at any point (animefillerlist types all 26 episodes Manga Canon) and the anime reaches the manga's true ending because volume 10 (the tankobon-only 'Period' and 'After' chapters) was published in April 2006, months before the anime finished. Chapter space is 83 units: chs 1-79 are the Weekly Shonen Jump run, ch 80 is 'Buso Renkin Finale' (65 pp, published in two installments in another Shueisha magazine), ch 81 is 'Buso Renkin Period' (86 pp, drawn for vol 10), ch 82 is the UNRELATED 'Embalming -Dead Body and Bride-' one-shot bundled in vol 10, and ch 83 is 'Buso Renkin After' (39 pp epilogue); MangaDex additionally carries 80.5/81.5 omake. Pace is very even: 1658 story pages over 26 episodes = ~64 pp/episode, i.e. 3-4 chapters an episode, which is exactly what the arc boundaries produce. No per-episode chapter source exists for this series anywhere (fandom is a stub wiki with empty chapter pages); every anchor below is DERIVED by triangulating (a) Japanese episode-title = chapter-title identity, (b) the archived official Xebec per-episode synopses, (c) the Buso Renkin Fandom wiki's per-character/per-location 'debut = Chapter N (Manga) / Episode M (Anime)' pairs, which pin 17 exact chapter-into-episode memberships, and (d) ja.wikipedia's explicit arc-to-chapter ranges (1-17 / 18-47 / 49-73 / 74-79+Final / vol 10). Episodes 18-20 (chs 57-70) are the one soft stretch and are marked medium with the reasoning stated.

anchors.note: Ep title = ch1 'New Life'; Saruwatari (the Haunted Factory homunculus boss Kazuki defeats at the end of ep1) has fandom debut ch2/ep1, and ch3's Koushaku+Washio debut in ep2, so ep1 ends exactly at ch2 'Midnight Run'.
Ep title = ch3 'Homunculus's Identity'; fandom debuts Koushaku Chouno + Washio ch3/ep2 and Kawazui ch4/ep2, while Hanabusa is ch5/ep3 - so ep2 = ch3-4 (Tokiko parasitised, ch4 'Parasite Homunculus').
Ep title = ch7 'You're a Little Stronger'; rose-homunculus Hanabusa debuts ch5/ep3 (fandom) and the Kawazui fight is ch5-6; Hotel Ginseikan is ch8/ep4, so ep3 closes vol 1 at ch7.

Ep title = ch9 'The Other New Life'; Hotel Ginseikan debuts ch8/ep4 (fandom). Official synopsis ends with Washio attacking = ch10 'VS. Washio Part 1', and ep5 opens mid-fight, so ep4 runs 8-10; the 10/11 split is inferred, not stated.

The three remaining 'VS. Washio' chapters (11-13). Squeezed: ep4 already contains ch10 and ep6 contains ch14 (Chouno Family Estate debut ch14/ep6), so 11-13 is the only fit; ep5 ends as Kazuki rides off for the antidote (the opening beat of ch14 'Midnight Run 2').

Three independent fandom debut markers land in ep6 - Chouno Family Estate ch14, Jiro/Shishaku Chouno ch15, Captain Bravo ch17 - and ja.wikipedia ends the Papillon-gang arc at ch17 (vols 1-2). Ep title = ch16 'Butterfly of Black Death'; ch17 'Fade to Black' is Koushaku's death + Bravo's arrival with the antidote.

Ep title = ch18 'If You Doubt That You Are A Hypocrite'; fandom puts Dr. Butterfly, Jinnai, Kinjo, Moonface and LXE HQ at ch18/ep7 and Lotteriya Burger at ch20/ep7. The Kinjo fight is the 'Kazuki and Tokiko's Choice' trilogy (19-21); ch22 is ep8's title chapter.

Ep title = ch22 'Night in the Dormitory'; Ouka Hayasaka debuts ch24/ep8 and Shusui ch25/ep9 (fandom), so ep8 ends exactly at ch24 'Destroy All Enemies' (Tokiko kills Jinnai, Papillon takes the kakugane).

Ep title = ch25 'The Hayasaka Siblings'; homunculi Tai and Shi (the pair that raid the school at the end of ep9) debut ch26/ep9. Ep10 opens with Kazuki reeling at the twins' identity, so ep9 ends on the reveal - placed at ch27 'Just the Two of Us'; the 27/28 boundary is derivation, not a stated fact.

Angel Gozen (Ouka's buso renkin) debuts ch30/ep10 and Mayumi Hayasaka ch31/ep11 (fandom), pinning the end at ch30 'Close Combat'; ep title 'Kimi to ore wa aisho ga ii' = ch29 'A Lot in Common' and the official caption quotes that line.

Mayumi Hayasaka debuts ch31/ep11 (fandom) = the twins' backstory (chs 31-32); ep ends with the hospital visit = ch34 'Let's o-Mimai / To the Hospital', and ep12 opens with the raid briefing = ch35 'Thirteen Hours to Go'.

Ep title = ch36 'Carnival'; fandom puts the Revised Humanoid Homunculi at ch36/ep12 and Shinyo Suzuki at ch37/ep12, so ep12 reaches at least 37. Ch38 'a friend of everybody' (the Bravo-vs-Moonface material) is assigned here on page budget (74 pp) and because ep13 opens on the school defence (ch39).

Ep title = ch40 'A Sign of Death'; Victor Powered debuts ch41/ep13 (fandom) and the episode ends with Papillon beating Dr. Butterfly = ch41-42 'Papillon vs. Butterfly' I-II. Ep14 starts by piercing the flask = ch43 (ep14's title chapter).

Ep title = ch43 'Who Are You?'; the Black Kakugane debuts ch44/ep14 (fandom). Ends at ch45 'A Spring Night of Two Months Past' (the flashback to Tokiko implanting the kakugane) = end of vol 5; ep15 opens with the Victorised Kazuki = ch46 'Heart Shift'.

Arc boundary: ja.wikipedia ends the LXE arc at ch47 ('End of the Battle' - Bravo vs Moonface settled, exactly the official ep15 synopsis) and starts the Alchemist-Army arc at ch49 with Bravo's beach revelation, leaving ch48 'A Warrior's Respite' (the beach day where Tokiko runs into Gouta) as ep15's close.

Ep title 'Arata naru chikara' mirrors ch49 'Arata naru ninmu / A New Mission'; the episode is Bravo's kill order through dumping Kazuki in the sea = chs 50 'Say It's Not So, Bravo', 51 'Crimson Ocean', 52 'Re-Extermination Complete'. Ep17's title is ch53 verbatim, fixing the boundary.

Ep title = ch53 'When the Night Ends' (Yo ga aketara); ch54 'One Heart and One Mind' is Tokiko reviving Kazuki, ch55 'Rainy Emotions' is Gouta wandering in the rain (verbatim in the official synopsis) and ch56 is his clash with the Re-Extermination Squad. Ep18's title = ch57 'Runaway Start'.

SOFT. Ep title = ch57 'Runaway Start'; the official synopsis ends as Papillon and Ikusabe square off, which fits ch61 'Which is MONSTER' with ch62 'Ikusabe Attacks' opening ep19. Derived from title identity + the ~4-chapter/episode pace of this arc (ja.wikipedia: arc = chs 49-73 over eps 16-21); no source states the boundary.

SOFT. Ep19 is Papillon finishing Ikusabe (chs 62 'Ikusabe Attacks' / 63 'Gekisen, the Cross Spear' - Gekisen is Ikusabe's buso renkin) plus Gouta beating Negoro, whose dimension-slipping ability is the subject of ch67 'Secret Passage of the Shadows'. Boundary derived, not stated.

The whole episode is Kazuki vs Captain Bravo round two: ch69 is literally 'Round Two' (their first bout was ep16) and ch70 'The Determination to Protect What's Important to the End' is the climax where Kazuki pierces Silver Skin; ep21 opens as Hiwatari bursts in (ch71).

Arc boundary. Ep title = ch72 'GONE INTO FLAME' (Hiwatari's napalm buso renkin Blaze of Glory); ja.wikipedia ends the Alchemist-Army arc at ch73 with exactly this episode's beats - Sakaguchi arrives, the situation is defused, Bravo is wounded by Hiwatari and leaves the front line ('Leave This to Me' = ch73).

Ep title = ch78 'Require a Decision'; the official synopsis runs ch74 'The Two Final Battles' (army's all-out attack on Victor) -> ch75 'Infiltrating Newton Apple Academy' (Victoria, fandom debut ch75) -> ch76 'Secret of the Mask' (the masked man from the underground space) -> ch77 'Great Battle' -> ch78, whose final image caption is the pair agonising over the choice they have been handed.

Ep title = ch79 'BOY MEETS BATTLE GIRL', the last WSJ chapter: the end-of-summer school day, everyone reunited, Kazuki alone on the roof water tank weighing the white kakugane. Ch79 is only 19 pp, so the parallel Victor-battle scenes are almost certainly lifted from the front of the 65-page 'Finale'; END held at 79 under the majority rule.

The 65-page 'Finale' chapter (vol 9, published Aug 2005 in two installments outside WSJ): summer festival, the finished white kakugane, the army pinned down over the Pacific, Sunlight Heart Plus, the white kakugane failing on Victor and Kazuki launching them both to the moon. ja.wikipedia scopes the Victor decisive-battle arc as 'vol 9, chs 74-79 + Final' ending on the moon.

ja.wikipedia's epilogue section is 'vol 10, Period / After, from one month after Kazuki and Victor vanished to the moon' - exactly the official ep25 synopsis (the army mopping up, Tokiko catatonic in hospital, then storming Papillon's lair to settle it in Kazuki's place). Ep25 covers roughly the first half of the 86-page ch81.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 81 ('Period', second half), 83 ('After'); ch 82 = the unrelated 'Embalming' one-shot, NOT adapted
anchors.note: Confirms the stored mu value of 83 but with the composition made explicit. Finale adapts the back half of ch81 'Period' (Papillon's white kakugane, Tokiko riding Buster Baron into space, Kazuki's return, the duel, Victor's restoration) and then ch83 'After' (39 pp - Papillon as urban legend, the pair back to ordinary life), which fan report says was carried largely by the closing/ED montage. Page budget supports real use of 'After': Period's back half alone is only ~43 pp against a 64 pp/episode series average.

continue_points.note: C1 mid-chapter: ep25 stops partway through the 86-page ch81 'Period' (Tokiko confronting Papillon), so the honest resume is ch81 itself.

Nothing left after ep26 except ch82, which is the unrelated 'Embalming -Dead Body and Bride-' one-shot bundled into vol 10; a reader wanting the real epilogue in print should read ch83 'After' (only montaged in the finale). If the app treats 83 as consumed, the series is simply complete.

annotations.note: The single 86-page tankobon-only chapter 'Buso Renkin Period' is split across two episodes (25 = grief + challenge to Papillon, 26 = white kakugane, rescue, duel, Victor's fate).
Ch83 'Buso Renkin After' (39 pp, drawn for vol 10) is condensed into the finale's closing/ED montage - Papillon as urban legend, Kazuki and Tokiko back to daily life.
Chapter 82 in the 83-unit numbering is the 'Embalming -Dead Body and Bride-' one-shot printed in vol 10; it is not Buso Renkin story content and is not adapted anywhere in the anime.
Ch80 'Finale' (65 pp) straddles two episodes: its opening Victor-battle material is intercut into ep23 around ch79, with the bulk of the chapter carried by ep24.

structure.notes: Single season, 26 episodes, our numbering = broadcast numbering 1:1 (component 1: anilist 1536, eps 1-26); no OVAs, movies or specials. animefillerlist types all 26 as Manga Canon ('Buso Renkin has no reported filler'), which matches the stored all-canon episode rows - no type corrections needed. CHAPTER SPACE (this resolves open flag #699): the reading edition is the 10-volume tankobon, whose 83 numbered units on AniList/MangaDex are chs 1-79 (Weekly Shonen Jump, Jun 2003 - Apr 2005), ch80 'Buso Renkin Finale' (65 pp, vol 9, published Aug 2005 in two installments in another Shueisha magazine), ch81 'Buso Renkin Period' (86 pp, vol 10 p.7), ch82 = the 'Embalming -Dead Body and Bride-' one-shot (vol 10 p.93, unrelated to the story), ch83 'Buso Renkin After' (vol 10 p.145, 39 pp); MangaDex also carries omake 80.5 and 81.5. MangaUpdates' 'latest chapter 39' is simply wrong/incomplete and should not be treated as a rival edition. VOLUME BOUNDARIES (identical on en.wikipedia, the Fandom chapter infoboxes and the MangaDex volume aggregate, and currently absent from our data): v1 1-7, v2 8-17, v3 18-26, v4 27-36, v5 37-45, v6 46-54, v7 55-63, v8 64-73, v9 74-80(+Finale), v10 80.5-83. ARC RANGES per ja.wikipedia: Papillon gang chs 1-17 (eps 1-6), LXE chs 18-47 (eps 7-15), Alchemist Army chs 49-73 (eps 16-21), Victor decisive battle chs 74-79+Finale (eps 22-24), epilogue vol 10 Period/After (eps 25-26). No Watsuki-side or Hiwatari-side divergence at the end: because vol 10 shipped in Apr 2006 and the anime ran Oct 2006 - Mar 2007, the adaptation lands on the manga's own ending rather than inventing one. Total story pages 1658 over 26 episodes = ~64 pp/episode, and every anchor above sits within a normal band of that.

flags_for_sean: SOURCE CEILING: no episode-to-chapter mapping exists for Buso Renkin anywhere - the Fandom wiki's chapter pages are empty stubs, animefillerguide has no page for the series, and Japanese searches turn up no correspondence table. Anchors are derived from (a) JP episode-title = chapter-title identity, (b) the archived official Xebec per-episode synopses (web.archive.org), (c) 17 Fandom 'debut = Chapter N (Manga) / Episode M (Anime)' pairs, (d) ja.wikipedia arc-to-chapter ranges. Anchors marked high are ones where a debut pair or an arc range pins the exact boundary; medium ones are content-derived.

WEAKEST STRETCH: eps 18-20 (chs 57-70). Ikusabe/Negoro/Hiwatari all have empty debut fields on the wiki, so the 61/62 and 67/68 boundaries are reasoned from chapter titles ('Which is MONSTER', 'Ikusabe Attacks', 'Secret Passage of the Shadows', 'Round Two') plus the arc's ~4-chapters-per-episode pace. Ep20 (Bravo round two, chs 68-70) and ep21 (chs 71-73) are the solid ends of that stretch.

MINOR CONFLICT resolved against Fandom: busorenkin.fandom's White Kakugane page says debut ch78 (Manga) / Episode 23 (Anime), but both en.wikipedia's ep22 summary and the official Xebec ep22 page (final caption: the two agonising over the choice they have been handed) put the white kakugane reveal and the choice in ep22. Anchored ep22 END = 78.

EP26 JUDGEMENT CALL: I kept the stored END = 83 rather than repairing to 81. Argument for 83: vol 10's story pages are Period 86 + After 39 = 125 over two episodes = 62 pp/ep, exactly series average, so 'After' supplied real content; ja.wikipedia's epilogue section and en.wikipedia's ep26 summary both end on 'Papillon becomes an urban legend / back to daily life', which is After material. Argument for 81: a fan blog reports the After material ran mostly over the ending credits, which under the finale rule ('never inflated to the furthest chapter touched') would be a sliver. If you prefer the stricter reading, set ep26 END = 81 and continue = 83.

OPEN FLAG #699 (MU 39 vs AniList 83): answer above in structure.notes - the tankobon/MangaDex 83-unit numbering is the reading edition and matches our stored total_chapters; MU's 39 is a bad record. Note the honest caveat that unit 82 is a non-Buso-Renkin one-shot, so '83 chapters' overstates story content by one unit.
